messages:
cheng: Heads up — after rolling kernel-selector v2 to prod last night we started seeing a big APAC prefix cache hit collapse. Quick snapshot: global hit 76% -> 73%, apac-east 79% -> 41%. EU/NA look unchanged. Deploy at 02:12 UTC, rollout finished ~02:45 UTC. Stack: dynamic_batch_v3 + kv-prefix-v1.

alex: Do we have perf counters/histograms? wondering if kernel changes triggered different execution paths (small-batch vs fused) or changed hashing behavior.

maria: Pulled the profiler and there's a ~2x increase in L3 misses during prefix hashing on p3d nodes in apac, plus a shift to the small-batch codepath for many requests. Sim runs link: https://dash.redwood/prof/1833 (internal). Sampling snapshot (simplified):
```
apac p3d kernel-selector-v1: prefix_hash_latency p50=1.2ms p99=3.1ms
apac p3d kernel-selector-v2: prefix_hash_latency p50=2.6ms p99=6.9ms
L3-miss-rate x2 on v2
```

deploy-bot: deploy kernel-selector-v2 @ 2026-04-12T02:12:00Z -> 80% -> full at 02:45. CI: green.

danny: Routing note: we briefly routed a subset of apac traffic to eu-west when node capacity spiked during rollout, then routed back. That caused cold-local caches in apac when traffic returned. Also saw replication queue backlog grow: replication-lag 8m -> 16m for prefix-sync.

cheng: I dug into key generation — there's a regression in PR #4221 (key-normalizer): we added canonicalization that lowercases and strips some unicode, but also switched to using tokenizer byte-prefix which changed hash inputs across the fleet. If regions compute different canonical bytes the replication layer won't match keys and misses skyrocket. I repro'd locally: same prompt => different cache key if tokenizer mode differs.

maria: Quick A/B sim: re-applying the stable canonicalizer (canonical_key_v1) in the key path fixes hit rate in our apac sim: simulated apac hit 76% -> 77% (back to baseline) and L3 misses drop. Patch diff (high level):
```
- key = normalize_v2(prompt)
+ key = canonicalize_bytes_v1(prompt)
```

alex: Can we avoid full rollback? short-term options: prefetch seeding + enable async replication for prefixes during failover window. I can script a prefetch: `scripts/seed_prefetch.sh --region=apac --window=24h --rate=500r/s` to warm hot keys.

danny: We can flip a routing flag so that when fallback occurs we enqueue async_replicate=true for prefix-sync for 1h after route-change. I'll add a policy toggle `replicate_on_routing: true` scoped to apac and set TTL 2h. That should reduce cold after re-routing. Also will prioritize replication queue on apac masters.

cheng: Action plan (short):
1) revert key-normalizer PR #4221 in canary (10%) now, roll to 50% if green.
2) enable `replicate_on_routing:true` for apac for 2h.
3) run alex's seed_prefetch script ASAP.
If we don't see APAC_prefix_hit > 60% by 10:30 UTC we'll rollback kernel-selector-v2 completely. I'll own the rollback timeline.

maria: Adding a temporary alert: APAC_prefix_hit < 60% for >5min -> pager to eng-runtime oncall. Also adding L3-miss-rate spike alert.

alex: +1. Will run the seed script and share logs here.

cheng: Thanks everyone — I'll coordinate the canary revert and follow up with a short postmortem after we stabilize.
